features.evidence: Sofwtare, gnireenignE, sdie
features.name: Mechanical polish
features.description: Captures how free the letter is from spelling, typographical, and copy-editing errors that distract from credibility.

levels.descriptor: Frequent obvious errors throughout, including in basic words or role names, making the letter feel careless.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the meaning remains recoverable without much effort.
Only a few minor slips appear and they do not seriously disrupt reading.
Clean or near-clean copy with no distracting mechanical mistakes.

features.evidence: Design ownership ... Extensive Python ... Proven work
features.name: Prose cohesion
features.description: Captures whether the letter reads as connected prose with clear flow rather than as a stack of disconnected claims.

levels.descriptor: Fragmented, list-like, or abruptly stitched together, with little sense of progression.
Understandable but choppy, with noticeable jumps between points.
Mostly smooth and readable, with a clear paragraph-to-paragraph flow.
Consistently fluid, well-structured prose that guides the reader naturally through the case.

features.evidence: replaced ad-hoc traversals with proper graph algorithms
features.name: Accomplishment specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter describes what the applicant built, changed, or investigated.

levels.descriptor: Mostly abstract claims, self-assessments, or buzzwords with little concrete evidence.
Some specific technologies or work areas are named, but responsibilities remain vague.
Several concrete examples make it clear what the applicant actually did.
Repeated vivid, technically grounded examples show exactly what was built or improved.

features.evidence: progressed from maintaining and testing production systems to launching 6 of them
features.name: Career trajectory
features.description: Captures whether the letter turns past experience into a coherent arc that makes this role feel like a logical next step.

levels.descriptor: No real arc; the letter reads like a flat inventory of qualifications.
Some chronology is present, but the connection between past work and this role is weak.
A clear progression, turning point, or buildup explains why this move makes sense now.
A memorable career arc ties earlier lessons directly to the responsibilities of this role.

features.evidence: the engineering problem I most want to spend the next several years on
features.name: Role targeting
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter connects the applicant to this exact security automation role rather than to software jobs in general.

levels.descriptor: Generic application language that could fit many software roles.
Broad interest in security or platform work is clear, but the fit remains general.
The letter explicitly connects to problems like secure defaults, vulnerability handling, or security automation.
The motivation is tightly tailored to this role's actual work, such as triage, variant analysis, agentic tooling, or secure SDLC support.

features.evidence: improvements there are inherited by every team downstream
features.name: Platform mindset
features.description: Captures how strongly the candidate frames impact in terms of foundational systems that benefit many teams rather than one product.

levels.descriptor: No shared-systems or organization-wide leverage perspective appears.
A larger-impact preference is implied but not developed.
The letter explicitly values central or foundational work that scales across teams.
Platform leverage is a core theme, supported by both past work and future motivation.

features.evidence: make the secure path the easy path for busy product engineers
features.name: Developer empathy
features.description: Captures whether the candidate frames security tooling as something that helps engineers by reducing friction rather than policing them.

levels.descriptor: No perspective on the developers who will use or live with the tooling.
General desire to help teams is stated, but without much detail.
The letter explicitly emphasizes secure defaults, toil reduction, or helping engineers move faster safely.
A strong builder-for-builders mindset appears, with concrete empathy for busy developer workflows and self-serve security.

features.evidence: Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, Doctoral degree
features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: Captures the highest relevant degree level the letter presents for technical preparation.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.evidence: 7 years ... launched 6 production services
features.name: Production tenure
features.description: Captures the depth of real software product experience shown through years worked and services tested, maintained, or launched.

levels.descriptor: Bare-minimum or thinly evidenced production experience.
Early-career record with some meaningful exposure to shipping or maintaining services.
Solid mid-level track record with multiple production systems across testing, maintenance, or launch.
Strong multi-year record with repeated launches and clear ownership of production work.
Especially extensive track record for this role, combining long tenure with many production services and clear lifecycle depth.

features.evidence: Go as my daily driver
features.name: Go fluency
features.description: Captures how central Go appears in the candidate's real work rather than being a peripheral language mention.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or mentioned so vaguely that real working fluency is unclear.
Go is listed among languages, but not presented as a main vehicle for important work.
Go is clearly a primary or daily language in the applicant's work.
Go is central to back-end ownership, infrastructure design, or safety-critical system boundaries the applicant built.

features.evidence: Python became my workhorse for everything operational
features.name: Python fluency
features.description: Captures the strength of the candidate's Python experience for tooling, automation, services, or prototypes.

levels.descriptor: Python is not mentioned.
Python is mentioned briefly, with little evidence of depth.
The letter shows regular Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is presented as extensive, production-grade, and central across tooling, services, or agent behavior.

features.evidence: automated vulnerability triage workflows
features.name: Vulnerability automation
features.description: Captures direct experience automating vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, or report handling.

levels.descriptor: No past vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in this problem, but gives no concrete example of having automated it.
A concrete example of triage, intake, routing, or report-handling automation is described.
The letter shows strong end-to-end automation of vulnerability handling, with clear workflow transformation or operational value.

features.evidence: Python agents real autonomy inside boundaries enforced by Go services
features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures experience designing systems in which agents perform multi-step work inside explicit technical guardrails.

levels.descriptor: No agentic-system experience appears.
Agents or agentic tooling are mentioned, but without meaningful architectural detail.
The letter describes a concrete agent-based system and the applicant's role in building it.
The letter shows clear design ownership of bounded, auditable agent systems, typically with explicit Go guardrails around Python agents.

features.evidence: learning to engineer around their failure modes
features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether AI experience is framed as dependable production engineering with evaluation or guardrails rather than as novelty alone.

levels.descriptor: No AI or LLM experience is mentioned.
AI is mentioned in general terms, with little evidence of production use.
The letter shows real experience shipping AI or LLM-backed features in production.
The letter emphasizes trustworthy deployment through evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or explicit failure-mode handling.

features.evidence: documenting findings and verifying their remediation
features.name: Security review practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues and following findings through design changes or fixes.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful security review or assessment experience is shown.
Security interest is signaled, but assessment work is vague or indirect.
The letter describes concrete security reviews, assessments, or threat models.
The letter shows substantial assessment practice with code review, attack-surface analysis, formal findings, or remediation follow-through.

features.evidence: cache eviction policies to dependency resolution
features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.evidence: maintainer of an open-source project with a genuine user community
features.name: Open-source ownership
features.description: Captures the degree of responsibility the candidate has taken in public codebases, from patches to full maintenance.

levels.descriptor: No open-source involvement is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional patches or upstream fixes.
The letter shows recurring contribution and some continuing responsibility.
The candidate presents maintainer-level ownership, including review, releases, roadmap, or community support.

features.evidence: finished near the top of several major events
features.name: Adversarial practice
features.description: Captures extracurricular offensive-security practice such as capture-the-flag participation and how serious it appears.

levels.descriptor: No adversarial practice is mentioned.
Occasional or casual participation is mentioned.
Regular participation shows a sustained habit of offensive practice.
Serious competitive involvement or strong placements signal unusually strong extracurricular offensive depth.

features.evidence: CompTIA Security+, OSCP
features.name: Security credentialing
features.description: Captures whether the letter includes third-party validation of security skills and how demanding that validation is.

levels.descriptor: No external security credential is mentioned.
A fundamentals-oriented credential such as Security+ is presented.
A more hands-on, advanced credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.evidence: built a distributed job scheduler with leader election and crash recovery
features.name: Side-project rigor
features.description: Captures how technically ambitious the candidate's personal projects appear and whether they reinforce systems or security depth.

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned, or only a very small generic app with little technical depth.
A modest personal build is described, but it does not show especially hard systems work.
A substantial systems or infrastructure project is described with meaningful engineering depth.
An ambitious distributed, fault-tolerant, or otherwise unforgiving project demonstrates serious self-driven technical rigor.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned to the team
features.name: Impact expression
features.description: Captures whether achievements are paired with a visible effect on workload, speed, coverage, or system quality rather than only being named.

levels.descriptor: Tasks are listed with no visible outcome or payoff.
Some benefit is implied, but the effect of the work remains vague.
The letter clearly states what got better because of the work.
The letter gives a memorable, concrete sense of value, making the outcome easy to picture.
